title: Electric potential (তড়িৎ বিভব)
placement: Book page 287, topic 10.6 তড়িৎ বিভব and 10.6.1 বিভব পার্থক্য, চিত্র ১০.১৪ (pp. 287–289).
description: Electric potential and potential difference (book pages 287–289, topics 10.6 and 10.6.1, চিত্র ১০.১৪). A polished steel sphere A with a positive charge q on a clear acrylic (insulating) stand, on a plain sand bench in a calm deep-blue setting, with a wooden rule in cm from A's centre; a small positive test charge q₀ on a carriage on a rail, on the line of চিত্র ১০.১৪. Honest lab sizes: q = 10 nC, q₀ = 2 nC, R = 5 cm, so V = 90/r (r in m). Five steps, one tap each: (1) q₀ is brought in at constant speed from the far end to r = 10 cm, the repulsion (teal) and the equal applied force (orange) grow as 1/r², and the panel's graph draws the work W from infinity; the student can then drag q₀ along the rail; (2) the work is divided by q₀: the same line's numbers become volts, V = W/q₀ = kq/r, and three equipotential shells (900, 450, 300 V) appear round A; (3) a second, uncharged sphere B stands at 30 cm, on the 300 V shell (A's field reaches it), and a wire joins them: negative electrons run from B to A, toward the higher potential, until both are at 1,050 V and the flow stops (the panel's columns level like water); (4) the book's crow lands on the wire, at the wire's potential: no difference, no shock; (5) an earthing cable joins B to the ground: electrons come up until A and B are at 0 V, the earth's potential. A calm intro card; per step the result and the rule in the book's words; the kit's drag handle, rotate cue and how-to row. Test tab: five questions read off the picture, each wrong choice with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
